intended_object: The ideal (det − 1) in the coordinate ring K[X_{ij}][1/det] of GL_n over a commutative ring K. The quotient by this ideal is the coordinate ring of SL_n. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and how the file uses the ideal.
explanation:
The body is `Ideal.span {(matrix K n).det - 1}`, taken inside `GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K n = Localization.Away (determinant K n)`. Here `matrix K n` is the universal matrix of variables X_{ij}, mapped into that localization. This is exactly the principal ideal (det − 1) of the localized GL coordinate ring, which is the defining ideal of SL_n.

Degenerate cases behave correctly. When n is empty, det = 1, so the ideal is 0 and SL_0 = GL_0. When K is the zero ring, everything is trivial.

The file goes on to prove that the ideal is a Hopf ideal and that the quotient is isomorphic to K[X_{ij}]/(det − 1). That isomorphism confirms the ideal is the intended one.

The setting (any commutative ring K, any finite index type with decidable equality) is the natural one; finiteness is needed for the determinant. Requiring n and K to share a universe is only a minor technical restriction.

Mathlib has no coordinate ring of GL_n or SL_n and no counterpart of this ideal. It provides the general Hopf-ideal machinery (`Ideal.IsHopfIdeal`), which the file uses.
